arxiv-2204-05763.title: Discretised Hilbert Space and Superdeterminism
arxiv-2204-05763.creator: T.N.Palmer
arxiv-2204-05763.description: Abstract In computational physics it is standard to approximate continuum systems with discretised representations. Here we consider a specific discretisation of the continuum complex Hilbert space of quantum mechanics - a discretisation where squared amplitudes and complex phases are rational numbers. The fineness of this discretisation is determined by a finite (prime-number) parameter p p .

arxiv-2209-12708.title: Faith: An Efficient Framework for Transformer Verification on GPUs
arxiv-2209-12708.creator: Boyuan Feng, Tianqi Tang, Yuke Wang, Zhaodong Chen, Zheng Wang, Shu Yang
arxiv-2209-12708.description: Abstract Transformer verification draws increasing attention in machine learning research and industry. It formally verifies the robustness of transformers against adversarial attacks such as exchanging words in a sentence with synonyms. However, the performance of transformer verification is still not satisfactory due to bound-centric computation which is significantly different from standard neural networks.

arxiv-2405-02408.title: Exomoons & Exorings with the Habitable Worlds Observatory I: On the Detection of Earth-Moon Analog Shadows & Eclipses Facilities: The Habitable Worlds Observatory
arxiv-2405-02408.creator: Mary Anne Limbach, Jacob Lustig-Yaeger, Andrew Vanderburg, Johanna M. Vos, René Heller, Tyler D. Robinson
arxiv-2405-02408.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mary Anne Limbach, Jacob Lustig-Yaeger, Andrew Vanderburg, Johanna M. Vos, René Heller, Tyler D. Robinson. The highest priority recommendation of the Astro2020 Decadal Survey for space-based astronomy was the construction of an observatory capable of characterizing habitable worlds. In this paper series we explore the detectability of and interference from exomoons and exorings serendipitously observed with the proposed Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) as it seeks to characterize exoplanets, starting in this manuscript with Earth-Moon analog mutual events.

arxiv-2407-03449.description: Abstract The advent of the sixth-generation (6G) networks presents another round of revolution for the mobile communication landscape, promising an immersive experience, robust reliability, minimal latency, extreme connectivity, ubiquitous coverage, and capabilities beyond communication, including intelligence and sensing. To achieve these ambitious goals, it is apparent that 6G networks need to incorporate the state-of-the-art technologies.

arxiv-2408-14239.title: Localized tension-induced giant folding in unstructured elastic sheets
arxiv-2408-14239.creator: Kexin Guo, Marc Suñé, Kwok Ming Li, K. Jimmy Hsia, Mingchao Liu, Dominic Vella
arxiv-2408-14239.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kexin Guo, Marc Suñé, Kwok Ming Li, K. Jimmy Hsia, Mingchao Liu, Dominic Vella. Buckling in compression is the archetype of elastic instability: when compressed along its longest dimension, a thin structure such as a playing card will buckle out-of-plane accommodating the imposed compression without a significant change of length. However, recent studies have demonstrated that tension applied to sheets with microscopic structure leads to out-of-plane deformation in applications from ‘groovy metasheets’ for multi-stable morphing to kirigami grippers.

pmc-10673201.title: Implementation of a Wideband Microwave Filter Design with Dual Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Mitigation for Modern Wireless Communication Systems with Low Insertion Loss and High Selectivity
pmc-10673201.creator: Abdul Basit, Amil Daraz, Guoqiang Zhang
pmc-10673201.description: By leveraging the advantages of the uniform transmission line, this manuscript presents a broadband high-selectivity filter range starting from 2.5 GHz to 16.8 GHz, utilizing a simple uniform transmission line structure loaded with three-quarter-wavelength stubs. The proposed UWB filter is studied using the ABCD network parameter method.

pmc-10711736.title: Experimental design of stencil-printed high-performance organic electrochemical transistors†
pmc-10711736.creator: Amir Mohammad Ghafari, Michele Catacchio, Emil Rosqvist, Axel Luukkonen, Anni Eklund, Kim Björkström, Paolo Bollella, Luisa Torsi, Eleonora Macchia, Ronald Österbacka
pmc-10711736.description: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are widely employed in several bioelectronic applications such as biosensors, logic circuits, and neuromorphic engineering, providing a seamless link between the realm of biology and electronics. More specifically, OECTs are endowed with remarkable signal amplification, the ability to operate in an aqueous environment, and the effective transduction of ionic to electrical signals.

pmc-12553437.title: Noninvasive Hemodynamic Characterization of Cardiohepatic Syndrome in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit
pmc-12553437.creator: Ahsan Butt, Mitchell Padkins, P. E. Miller, Jason N. Katz, Dustin B. Hillerson, Drew N. Rosenbaum, Marc D. Samsky, Maan Jokhadar, Jacob C. Jentzer
pmc-12553437.description: BackgroundPatients with cardiohepatic syndrome are at higher risk of adverse outcomes in the cardiac intensive care unit. We hypothesized that cardiohepatic syndrome phenotypes would exhibit differences in their clinical and transthoracic echocardiogram hemodynamic profiles, portending a higher risk of mortality.

pmc-12669381.title: Intelligent Nanomedicine Systems Utilizing Diverse Nanoparticles for Osteosarcoma Therapy: A Review
pmc-12669381.creator: Jie Cai, Hulin Yang, Zongxian He, Chenghu Wu
pmc-12669381.description: Osteosarcoma and other solid tumor therapies remain urgent clinical challenges. Currently, treatment mainly relies on surgical resection. However, surgery often requires extensive removal of bone and surrounding tissues, which can easily lead to impaired limb function, affect patients’ immune and metabolic functions, and increase the risk of recurrence. Smart nanomedicine offers new hope for the treatment of solid tumors.

pmc-12681448.title: The Role of Ultrasonography and Magnetic Resonance Imaging in the Evaluation of Adnexal Masses With Histopathological Correlation
pmc-12681448.creator: Chethana S Reddy, A Baskar, M Kalaichezhian, G Murugan
pmc-12681448.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Accurate evaluation of adnexal masses is crucial for appropriate management, distinguishing benign from malignant lesions, and guiding surgical planning. Ultrasonography (USG) is commonly used as a first-line modality, while magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides detailed tissue characterization. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of USG and MRI in the assessment of adnexal masses and to correlate imaging findings with histopathological examination (HPE).Methods: A prospective study was conducted on 67 patients presenting with adnexal masses.

pmc-12689079.title: Seborrheic Keratosis of the Nasal Vestibule: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-12689079.creator: Jee Won Moon, Tae Sung Jeon, Heung-Man Lee
pmc-12689079.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Seborrheic keratosis (SK) is a common benign epithelial neoplasm most often found on sun-exposed skin, particularly in elderly individuals. Despite its prevalence, involvement of the nasal vestibule is extraordinarily rare, with only a few documented cases. We present the case of a 59-year-old man with a verrucous lesion in the left nasal vestibule that was completely excised and histopathologically confirmed as SK.

pmc-13171843.title: Effect of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation on perioperative hypothermia in video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13171843.creator: Yajie Zhao, Hansheng Liang, Kaidi Kang, Menghan Su, Qian Gao, Yaqing Wu, Weixin Zhang, Yue Li, Liang Sun, Yi Feng
pmc-13171843.description: BackgroundPerioperative hypothermia is common during video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) is a noninvasive neuromodulation technique that may modulate thermoregulation; however, evidence from randomized controlled trials remains limited. This study evaluated whether TEAS prevents perioperative hypothermia in patients undergoing VATS.

pmc-13376097.title: Isolation, characterization, and in vitro efficacy of phage Citro-6 against Citrobacter freundii-induced bovine mastitis
pmc-13376097.creator: Ziyi Wang, Hong Li, Rihua Xu, Ke Meng, Jun Zhu
pmc-13376097.description: IntroductionBovine mastitis is a prevalent infectious disease in dairy herds worldwide, resulting in substantial economic losses. Citrobacter freundii has emerged as an opportunistic pathogen associated with mastitis, and its increasing antibiotic resistance poses significant therapeutic challenges.MethodsIn this study, a novel lytic phage, Citro-6, was isolated from dairy farm sewage and fecal samples using C. freundii Z6 as the host bacterium.

pmc-13578387.title: Fibroblast Growth Factor 21: Possible Role in Growth and Metabolic Development during Early Life, Nutritional Interactions and Biological Actions
pmc-13578387.creator: Jibran A Wali, José Manuel Ramos-Nieves, Aristea Binia, Eline M van der Beek
pmc-13578387.description: Fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) is a hormone produced mainly in the liver that plays a crucial role in systemic metabolic regulation. Its diverse metabolic functions include promoting glucose uptake in adipocytes, enhancing fat oxidation, and inducing thermogenesis. Studies in rodents have shown that treatment with FGF21 protects against diet-induced obesity and when overexpressed, can even extend lifespan.
